rv.q: With stellar performances across the cast and particularly magnetic work from Anna Crichlow as Hortense and Bronté Barbé as Queenie, this is a necessary history play that feels all too contemporary.
Matthew Xia's production of Helen Edmundson's adaptation of Andrea Levy's saga of the Windrush generation is wonderfully involving.

Fortunately, while this version cannot fully replicate the expansiveness of its predecessor, it nevertheless succeeds as a thrilling piece of narrative theatre, full of engaging and vividly realised characters.
Helen Edmundson’s adaptation of Andrea Levy’s novel gets a wonderfully performed, visually expansive regional premiere
It’s monumental theatre on a national scale and, whatever its flaws, it demands your attention.
This astounding production adapted by Helen Edmundson and directed by Olivier Award winning Matthew Xia, is a journey you really don’t want to miss.

cn.t: Matthew Xia's production of Helen Edmundson's adaptation earns praise for its stellar performances and involving storytelling, bringing Andrea Levy's Windrush epic to life with clarity and relevance for contemporary audiences.
